identity.title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoints Stimulation Improves Spontaneous Voiding Recovery After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Randomized Clinical Trial
identity.read_pages: 1–10 complete; visual flow p4 and Tables1/4 pp5/7; official NCT03631160 current record

arms.protocol: Strongest tolerated 2Hz BL32/SP6/CV3/CV4, 30min preinduction to45min postsurgery; sham cut wires/no current, identical device sound/lights.

pain.location: Table4 p7; registry describes rest and cough at6–8h, not24h

vomiting.location: Table4 p7; vomiting alone, not composite PONV

opioid.unit: mg IV morphine equivalents, author converted

voiding.unit: hours end-surgery to first spontaneous void

opioid.drug: sufentanil administered; reported outcome is author-converted IV morphine equivalents
opioid.pca: IV sufentanil plus flurbiprofen,24–48h as needed; concentration/settings not reported
opioid.reason: 48h median/IQR is not exact0–24h and not mean/SD. Author cites ClinCalc conversion without raw constituent doses/factors; no independent conversion performed.

source_conflicts: Table2 voiding TEAS IQR upper8.0 vs abstract8.1; control median7.1 vs abstract7.0; retain table provenance.
Current registry describes planned multicenter1200, nonacupoint sham and2/100Hz, versus publication single-center1948 and2Hz same-acupoint sham. Amendment history not retrieved.
Registry pain rest/cough6–8h but publication collapses to one unspecified NRS. No exact24h support.

registration.prespecification: Prospective registration established; original version and timely SAP not available. Current record alone does not establish original exact analysis.

D1.evidence: Methods pp2–3 computer block randomization and sequential opaque sealed numbered envelopes opened by acupuncturist after enrollment; baseline table has no clear randomization failure.

D2.evidence: Methods pp2–4 active strongest-tolerated stimulation versus no-current sham; acupuncturist knows, patients told sensation may vary; care and assessors masked. No documented trial-context deviations; analyzed participants retained assignment. Postrandomization missing outcomes evaluated in D3.

D3.evidence: Flow p4:53/975 and57/973 excluded: canceled surgery20/29, insensitive2/1, otherclinical2/0, conversion10/7, intraopcatheter19/20. 110 missing; procedure/catheter changes could relate to pain,opioid,urination/vomiting; no ITT sensitivity, actual missing-value dependence unknown.

D4.evidence: Methods and Table4: patient pain reports and vomiting/voiding records can be affected by perceived stimulation; assessment procedures equal and personnel masked, but sensory masking not demonstrated. Actual influence not established.

D4_opioid.evidence: Table1 and methods: dose from perioperative administration records assessed by masked personnel. Self-dosing is distinct from inaccurate recording. Conversion completeness is an endpoint-validity limitation, not automatic detection bias.

D5.evidence: NCT03631160 prospectively posted15Aug2018; current record updatedMay2021. No original SAP/history. Registered rest/cough NRS6–8h collapsed into unspecified result; multiple possible measurements/analyses, result-based selection unproven.

independence: Nankai cholecystectomy Aug2018–Jun2020 cohort, registration NCT03631160; not the hysterectomy/gynecologic cohorts. Registry-linked report is same trial, not separate independent data.
